references.text: Moses hid his face because he was afraid to look at God—the same sense of unworthiness and holy fear that Simon Peter shows toward Jesus.
Gideon feared he would die because he had seen the angel of the Lord face to face—a parallel to Peter's experience of standing near the holy.

Isaiah cries out, 'Woe is me! I am lost, for I am a man of unclean lips' when he sees the glory of the Lord—a very close parallel to Peter's confession of his sinfulness in the presence of Jesus' divine power.
Job says that he had heard about God with his ears, but now his eye sees him, and therefore he repents in dust and ashes—recognition of his own unworthiness in God's presence, like Peter's reaction.
The context for Peter's reaction: the miraculous catch of fish that made Peter realize Jesus' divine power.
The officer in Capernaum felt unworthy for Jesus to come under his roof—a similar humility and recognition of Jesus' greatness.
The tax collector who struck his breast and said, 'God, be merciful to me, a sinner!'—a parallel confession of sinfulness in the presence of the holy.
John fell down as dead at Jesus' feet when he saw the glorified Christ—the same reaction of holy fear and awe that Peter showed.
The disciples fell down and worshiped Jesus after he walked on water—an acknowledgment of his divinity, like Peter's reaction after the miraculous catch.
Ezekiel fell on his face when he saw the glory of the Lord—a response of awe and submission similar to Peter's reaction.

When the ark of the covenant returned, the Lord struck down the people of Beth-Shemesh, and they said, 'Who can stand before the Lord, this holy God?'—recognition of unworthiness in the presence of God's holiness.
Abraham says to the Lord, 'Behold, I have undertaken to speak to the Lord, although I am but dust and ashes'—a humble recognition of his own insignificance before God.
